title: The Little Gray Bug in Your Basement Isn't a Bug

beats.say: Touch the little armored bug in your basement, and it locks itself into a ball.
And it isn't even an insect. It's a crustacean, a cousin of crabs and shrimp.
The pillbug. Seven pairs of legs, and plates of armor.
It rolls up to protect itself, and to hold in water.
Its cousin, the sowbug, can't roll up. It has two little tails instead.
It eats dead leaves, rotting plants, and fungus.
Its group are the only crustaceans that fully moved onto land.
It comes inside looking for water, into basements and crawl spaces.
But in a dry house, it struggles to survive.
It doesn't bite or sting. It's harmless to people and pets.
The mom carries her eggs and babies in a pouch, called a marsupium.
It can live about three years.
Outside, it's a helper. It recycles dead plants back into the soil.
Sometimes, though, it nibbles young seedlings.
Its back is seven hard plates, overlapping like armor.
Indoors, it usually shows up in basements and ground floor rooms.
Would you let one crawl on your hand?
Follow me. Part twenty four runs across your floor at night.
